summary.text: A 27-hole Robert Trent Jones Jr redesign of Frank Pennink's 1975 course at Lagos, laid out as three nines called Alvor, Lagos and Praia.

setting.text: Sits between the Bay of Lagos and the Alvor Estuary, with views over both.
The clubhouse looks over the Alvor Estuary, Meia Praia beach and Ponta da Piedade.
European Tour Destinations describes Alvor as traditional parkland, Praia as true links, and Lagos as heathland acting as a transition between them.
Alvor runs through pine-lined corridors, with most holes climbing hillsides or dropping through narrow valleys.
Golf Course Architecture says the Alvor nine is mostly inland, with steeper terrain and the course's most severe greens.
Golf Course Architecture picks out a pretty par 3 near the water as the highlight of the Alvor nine.
The Praia nine is a seaside dune setting, fully exposed to the elements, with four holes alongside the beach and a railway line.
The Lagos nine starts in parkland and has the only two lakes on the whole site.
On the inland side of the Tunes to Lagos railway line, newly bought land was shaped to resemble links.
That area holds a double green modelled on the 7th and 11th at the Old Course at St Andrews, including a replica of the Eden par 3.

history.text: Frank Pennink, an Anglo-Dutch architect, designed the original course, which opened in 1975.
The original was best known for five holes beside the Atlantic, the nearest thing to links golf in the Algarve at the time.
Portuguese firm Onyria, owner of Quinta da Marinha near Lisbon, bought Palmares in 2003 and hired Robert Trent Jones Jr's practice.
Golf Course Architecture reported the reconstructed 27 holes open in June 2011.
European Tour Destinations says 18 holes opened in October 2010 and the full 27 were complete in June 2011.
Jones said the aim was to let the land determine the look rather than impose a signature style, and that Palmares has 'multiple personalities'.
The clubhouse was designed by RCR Arquitectes, winners of the Pritzker Architecture Prize.

trivia.text: Top100golfcourses lists the Praia & Lagos combination, and its 2026 Portugal Top 50 write-up places Palmares inside the top eight.
Top100golfcourses calls Palmares the 'jewel in the crown of the Algarve', and says it offers one of the best views of any Portuguese course.
The three nines can be combined as desired, giving a different 18 each time.
The driving range is 300 metres long.
Where2golf lists the Lagos/Praia combination at 6,314 metres from the back tees, par 72.

2.text: The second hole takes golfers down into true coastal links, which then runs to the closing hole, says Portugalgolf.

9.text: A strong uphill par 5 rising out of the dunes through a deep valley to an amphitheatre just below the clubhouse, per Portugalgolf.

12.text: The first three Alvor holes occupy the least interesting land on the site, but Golf Course Architecture rates the third green as excellent.

15.text: The sixth and seventh give a preview of the dune holes to come, according to Portugalgolf.

16.text: Together with the sixth, gives a preview of the dune holes to come, according to Portugalgolf.

17.text: The Alvor nine ends with a stiff climb up the eighth and ninth back to the clubhouse, says Golf Course Architecture.

18.text: The last of a stiff climb back to the clubhouse that begins on the eighth.

local.text: Palmares is near Meia Praia beach at Lagos, about 45 minutes' drive from Faro airport.
Meia Praia is described as one of the largest open bays in Europe, and is Lagos's most popular tourist beach.
Lagos was a centre of the Age of Discovery and a frequent home of Henry the Navigator.
Ponta da Piedade, a rock formation near Lagos, is one of the area's best-known sights.
